title: US Makes Visa Bond Program Permanent, Raises Maximum to $20,000 — India Not on List
excerpt: The State Department's final rule takes effect today, requiring applicants from 50 countries to post refundable bonds of up to $20,000 for B1/B2 visas. India remains excluded from the program.
body:
• The US has made its visa bond pilot program permanent, raising the maximum bond from $15,000 to $20,000 for B1 and B2 visa applicants from 50 countries.
  • India is not on the list of affected countries, but South Asian neighbors Bangladesh, Nepal, and Bhutan are included.
  • The final rule, published in the Federal Register on August 3, eliminates the $5,000 bond option, leaving $10,000, $15,000, and $20,000 as the three tiers.

The US State Department has made its visa bond program permanent, according to a Federal Register notice published on Friday. The final rule, which takes effect today, August 3, raises the maximum bond to $20,000 and applies to citizens of 50 countries seeking B1 (business) or B2 (tourism) visas.

"Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers," the notice said, according to Reuters.

From Pilot to Permanent

The program began as a pilot in August 2025 under the Trump administration, initially offering consular officers three bond options: $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000. The list started with around two dozen countries and expanded in phases — first to 38 nations by January 2026, then to 50 in April 2026 when 12 more countries, including Cambodia, Ethiopia, and Tunisia, were added.

https://x.com/stats_wire/status/2083560932660199489

The final rule eliminates the $5,000 tier. Consular officers now choose between $10,000, $15,000, and $20,000, based on the applicant's travel history, ties to their home country, and the overstay rates associated with their nationality.

"The 2025 visa bond pilot has provided sufficient data to suggest that a visa bond program is an effective tool for enforcing compliance among bonded visa holders."

— US State Department, Federal Register notice

The bonds are refundable. Travelers who depart the United States within their authorized stay period receive a full refund. Those who overstay forfeit the entire amount.

Which Countries Are Affected?

Of the 50 countries on the list, 30 are in Africa. The roster includes Nigeria, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Cuba, Venezuela, Ethiopia, and Fiji, among others. Countries were selected based on B1/B2 overstay rates from Department of Homeland Security data, as well as assessments of screening and vetting capacity.

Bonded visa holders must enter and exit the United States through commercial air ports of entry only — charter flights, general aviation, and land or sea crossings are not permitted.

India Excluded — But Neighbors Are Not

India does not appear on the list of 50 countries, a point of relief for the millions of Indians who apply for US tourist and business visas each year. Analysts attribute the exclusion to India's relatively lower B1/B2 overstay rates compared to the listed nations.

However, neighboring South Asian countries tell a different story. Bangladesh and Nepal have been subject to the bond requirement since January 21, 2026, while Bhutan was added on January 1, 2026. For Indian Americans with family ties across South Asia, the program's reach into the subcontinent remains a concern.

The financial burden is substantial. For a Bangladeshi or Nepali applicant, a $15,000 or $20,000 bond — even if refundable — represents a major barrier. Each family member applying for a visa may need to post a separate bond, potentially pushing the total deposit for a family of four to $60,000 or more.

Criticism and Context

Immigration advocates have argued the program deters legitimate travel to the United States. Rights groups say the Trump administration's broader immigration crackdown violates due process and disproportionately targets ethnic minorities.

"Trump's immigration policies have led some visitors to skip travel to the United States."

— Reuters

The administration has defended the measures as necessary for national security, pointing to a 2023 DHS report that found more than 314,000 B1/B2 visa overstays. Trump has simultaneously imposed social media vetting for visa applicants and a travel ban blocking citizens of 19 nations on security grounds.

What's Next

With the program now permanent, the State Department retains the authority to add or remove countries from the list as overstay data evolves. The elimination of the $5,000 tier and the increase to a $20,000 maximum signal an escalation in enforcement intensity. For Indian travelers, the exclusion provides breathing room — but for the broader South Asian community and the 50 affected nations, the cost of visiting America just went up.
nri_angle: India is excluded from the visa bond list, providing relief for Indian travelers, but neighboring Bangladesh, Nepal, and Bhutan are affected, impacting the broader South Asian community.
